_why: Tim, 2026-09-08: 'if there isn't something to reap old work trees, that's definitely something that we can add to the MCP server... it's already a long-lived process.. just remove anything more than 48 hours old.' The server is the thing that can do it without anyone remembering to, which is the point — a teardown step in a brief is a step that will eventually not happen, and D1 (a reviewer authors its fix in its own worktree) turns the leak from incidental into one per review round. Measured that day: three orphans already, one from a dead session and two from probe runs that did not tear down.
_two_horizons: Tim, 2026-09-08, asked for clean at 48h and DIRTY AT 7 DAYS. A dirty worktree may hold uncommitted work, and destroying uncommitted work while reporting success is this project's archetypal failure — the reason reset --hard, clean and stash are refused outright. Commits survive reaping (a detached worktree's objects live in the shared store), so the exposure is narrow and specific: a reviewer that authored a fix and never committed it. Seven days is the grace that makes it discoverable instead of gone.
_session_state_is_not_work: ⛔ WHAT MAKES THE 48h HORIZON REACHABLE AT ALL, and the reasoning survives the field's move to `GitRobot._SESSION_STATE`. Tim, 2026-09-08: gate_round.json is 'a session State tracking variable' — tracked in git at {round: 0} and rewritten at runtime with arc_base/targets/reset_from, so it is dirty essentially always. Counting it would mark EVERY worktree dirty and nothing would ever take the 48h path. This is not a tolerance for a file we allow to be dirty: the reaper's question is 'does this tree hold work someone would lose', and session state is not work. A path listed here has its dirtiness treated as carrying no information.
_not_hardcoded: Config rather than a literal because session-state-in-a-tracked-file is a PATTERN, not one file. The next one must not need a code change.
_session_state_moved: MOVED TO `GitRobot._SESSION_STATE` 2026-09-13. It was a THIRD declaration of the same fact — `_ARC_STATE` and `_EXPECTED_LOCAL` in engine.py were the other two — and the one furthest from the guards that depend on it. Membership is a STRUCTURAL FACT the guards read; an absent list would make them treat a live counter as WORK and refuse every branch move. The horizons stay here because they are TUNABLE POLICY the gated party must not set, and an absent config correctly DISABLES the reaper rather than defaulting one. ⚠ Do not re-add this key: a config value the code ignores is a fourth copy that reads as authority.
